techStack.notes: pnpm monorepo. Packages: openvole (src/core), @openvole/paw-sdk, @openvole/volenet, @openvole/dashboard-server, volenet-mcp. Paws live in a separate repository. Agent loop is LLM-agnostic; brain, tools, and channels are out-of-process paws. pnpm-lock.yaml was excluded from the scan.

issues.title: Panel tool route skips the session token
issues.description: POST /panel/<agent>/<paw>/tool/<name> executes a paw tool after checking only that the Origin host equals the Host header. It does not check the dashboard session token. Origin is client-supplied, so any process that can reach the port (the server binds 0.0.0.0 by default) can set both headers and call tools. The comment says a token-less curl cannot do this; a non-browser client can. docs/security.md says the token is what makes reaching the port insufficient, and that panel routes require it.
issues.suggestion: Require tokenOk(req) on the tool POST the same way the WebSocket and the panel HTML route do. Keep the Origin check as CSRF defense, not as a substitute for the token.

issues.title: Docker sandbox mounts the whole .openvole directory
issues.description: The Node permission sandbox deliberately does not grant .openvole/ wholesale, because that directory holds the vault and VoleNet private keys. The Docker path, which docs/security.md recommends for untrusted paws, bind-mounts the entire .openvole directory read-only at /openvole. Every paw container can read vault.json, vole_key, and other paws' data. The permissions argument is unused, so filesystem grants are not applied.
issues.suggestion: Mount only the paw data directory (and any path in the effective filesystem grant). Do not mount .openvole/net or the vault into the container.

issues.title: Unreadable vault is treated as empty and can be overwritten
issues.description: init() uses one catch for a missing file, a permissions error, and invalid JSON. All three start from an empty map. The next store() calls save(), which rewrites vault.json with only the new entry and drops every secret that was already on disk.
issues.suggestion: Treat ENOENT as an empty vault. On parse or permission errors, throw and refuse to save so a later store() cannot clobber the file.

issues.title: A corrupt vole.config.json is rewritten as empty
issues.description: readConfigFile() returns {} when the file is missing or when JSON.parse throws. addPawToConfig, removePawFromConfig, addSkillToConfig, and removeSkillFromConfig all read through this helper and then write the object back. A truncated or invalid vole.config.json therefore loses brain, security, net, and the existing paw list on the next paw or skill install.
issues.suggestion: Return {} only for ENOENT. If the file exists but does not parse, throw and do not call writeConfigFile.

issues.title: Invalid vole.config.json is loaded as defaults
issues.description: loadUserConfig() catches JSON parse failures and falls through to JS module candidates, then to built-in defaults. A present but invalid vole.config.json is indistinguishable from "no config": paws, security.allowedPaths, and net settings are dropped, and the process continues. The warning is only printed after every candidate fails, and it says the file was not found.
issues.suggestion: If vole.config.json exists, fail startup on parse errors. Only use defaults when the file is absent.

issues.title: Vault key is a raw SHA-256 and the file is not mode 0600
issues.description: VOLE_VAULT_KEY is hashed once with SHA-256 and used as an AES-256-GCM key. There is no salt and no slow KDF, so a leaked vault.json is open to a fast dictionary attack. save() writes the file with the process umask, unlike vole_key and the dashboard token, which are created mode 0600. When VOLE_VAULT_KEY is unset, values are stored as plaintext and only a debug log says so.
issues.suggestion: Derive the key with scrypt or PBKDF2 and a stored salt. Write vault.json with mode 0o600. Refuse to start, or warn loudly, when VOLE_VAULT_KEY is unset.

issues.title: Security doc overstates the dashboard token check
issues.description: The security page says the session token is required on panel routes, so reaching the port is not enough to control the dashboard, and that same-origin checks block token-less tool calls. The panel HTML route checks the token. The panel tool POST checks only Origin versus Host and does not check the token. That is the opposite of the guarantee this section states.
issues.codeSnippet:
- **Session token.** ... The token is required on the page, the WebSocket, and panel routes, so reaching the port is **not** enough to control the dashboard.
- **Same-origin enforcement.** The WebSocket and panel-tool routes require a matching `Origin`, blocking cross-site WebSocket hijacking and token-less cross-site tool calls.
issues.suggestion: After the tool route requires the token, keep this text. Until then, document that panel tool POSTs are authorized by a client-supplied Origin header.

issues.title: Dashboard UI is a 7,152-line HTML string
issues.description: getDashboardHtml returns one template literal that contains the full dashboard markup, CSS, and client script. A change to chat, projects, or VoleNet UI means editing the same function, and the file cannot be typechecked or unit-tested as modules.
issues.suggestion: Split the client into separate modules (or at least separate template files per panel) that the server concatenates. Keep the zero-dependency delivery if that constraint still matters.

issues.title: VoleNetManager is a 3,403-line god module
issues.description: src/volenet/src/index.ts owns discovery wiring, tool calls, chat, relay, rooms, file transfer, and session sync in one class. Message handlers are a long if/else chain. A bug in one path is hard to isolate, and tests reach into private fields with casts because there is no smaller surface.
issues.codeSnippet:
// src/volenet/src/index.ts — 3,403 lines
// VoleNetManager handles discovery, tools, chat, relay, rooms, and files.
issues.suggestion: Move each message family (chat, files, relay, rooms) into the modules that already exist beside this file, and leave index.ts as lifecycle and dispatch.

issues.title: CLI entrypoint is 2,636 lines of every subcommand
issues.description: src/core/src/cli.ts implements init, paw and skill scaffolding, serve, upgrade, and dashboard token setup in one file. Command handlers cannot be tested without loading the whole entrypoint, and unrelated changes conflict in the same module.
issues.suggestion: Split each subcommand into its own module and keep cli.ts as argument parsing and dispatch.

issues.title: VoleNet is published on globalThis as any
issues.description: Startup assigns the manager to (globalThis as any).__volenet__. Core loop, core tools, the paw registry, and the control adapter then read that property through the same cast. A renamed method or a missing isActive() compiles cleanly and fails only when a tool runs. The cast is repeated at more than a dozen call sites.
issues.codeSnippet:
// Make VoleNet accessible to core tools via globalThis
;(globalThis as any).__volenet__ = this
issues.suggestion: Pass the VoleNet manager into the engine and tool context as a typed interface. If a global is still required, declare it in one .d.ts and stop using as any at the call sites.

issues.title: Dashboard token persistence failures are ignored
issues.description: When VOLE_DASHBOARD_TOKEN is unset and no token file exists, vole serve generates a token and writes <root>/.openvole/dashboard-token mode 0600. Both mkdir and writeFile swallow errors. The server still starts and prints a URL. The next start generates a different token, and the operator is not told the file was never written.
issues.codeSnippet:
token = randomBytes(24).toString('hex')
await fs.mkdir(path.dirname(tokenFile), { recursive: true }).catch(() => {})
await fs.writeFile(tokenFile, `${token}\n`, { mode: 0o600 }).catch(() => {})
issues.suggestion: Log and exit if the token file cannot be created. A dashboard that starts without a persisted token should not look the same as a successful start.
